data.title: Outcomes of tranexamic acid administration in military trauma patients with intracranial hemorrhage: a cohort study
data.author: Walker

available_outcomes.name: Underwent cranial decompression
available_outcomes.source_quote: Table 3 Outcomes stratified by tranexamic acid administration... Underwent cranial decompression, n: TXA (n = 14) 7 (50.0%); No TXA (n = 57) 24 (42.1%)

available_outcomes.name: Field GCS
available_outcomes.source_quote: Table 3 Outcomes stratified by tranexamic acid administration... Field GCS: TXA (n = 14) 9.2 ± 4.4; No TXA (n = 57) 12.5 ± 3.4. Continuous variables expressed as mean ± standard deviation

available_outcomes.name: Discharge GCS
available_outcomes.source_quote: Table 3 Outcomes stratified by tranexamic acid administration... Discharge GCS: TXA (n = 14) 13.3 ± 4.0; No TXA (n = 57) 13.8 ± 3.2. Continuous variables expressed as mean ± standard deviation

available_outcomes.name: Change in GCS
available_outcomes.source_quote: Table 3 Outcomes stratified by tranexamic acid administration... Change in GCS: TXA (n = 14) 3.7 ± 3.9; No TXA (n = 57) 1.3 ± 3.1. Continuous variables expressed as mean ± standard deviation

available_outcomes.source_quote: Table 3 Outcomes stratified by tranexamic acid administration... 6-month GOS: TXA (n = 14) 3.5 ± 0.9; No TXA (n = 57) 3.8 ± 1.0. Continuous variables expressed as mean ± standard deviation

available_outcomes.name: Mortality
available_outcomes.source_quote: Table 3 Outcomes stratified by tranexamic acid administration... Mortality, n: TXA (n = 14) 1 (7.1%); No TXA (n = 57) 4 (7.0%)

available_outcomes.name: Progression of ICH
available_outcomes.source_quote: Of the 45 patients with an interval CT scan prior to intervention available for analysis, 11 (24.4%) demonstrated progression of ICH (Table 4)... although there was a trend towards a higher rate of progression in those patients that received TXA (45.5% vs. 14.7%, p = 0.09). Table 4... TXA administration, n: Total (n=45) 10 (22.2%); ICH Progression (n=11) 5 (45.5%); No ICH Progression (n=34) 5 (14.7%). [Calculated from table columns: 5/10 TXA progressed vs 6/35 No TXA progressed].

available_outcomes.name: Venous thromboembolism (VTE)
available_outcomes.source_quote: Nine patients in the cohort (12.7%) were diagnosed with VTE (Table 5)... [They] were also more likely to have ... been administered TXA (55.6% vs. 14.5%, p = 0.01). Table 5... Administered TXA, n: VTE (n=9) 5 (55.6%); No VTE (n=62) 9 (14.5%). [Thus among 14 TXA patients, 5 had VTE; among 57 No TXA patients, 4 had VTE].

quotes.confounding: Patients that received TXA were more severely injured (36.6 ± 12.5 vs. 26.2 ± 11.4, p = 0.003)... lower initial reported GCS (9.2 ± 4.4 vs. 12.5 ± 3.4, p = 0.008)
quotes.selection: Patients were only included if they survived evacuation to the Continental United States, potentially excluding patients who had worse overall outcomes.
quotes.classification: Results were stratified based on TXA administration, progression of ICH, and VTE.
quotes.deviations: Data was obtained from the Department of Defense Trauma Registry (DoDTR)...
quotes.missingData: Patients were excluded if they... had incomplete data. 26 patients (36.7%) underwent cranial decompression prior to their follow-up CT scan and therefore were excluded from determination of ICH progression.
quotes.measurement: Progression of ICH was determined qualitatively based on radiologist interpretation.
quotes.reporting: Data collected included: demographics, types of injuries, initial and interval head computerized tomography (CT) scans, Glasgow Coma Scores (GCS), and six-month Glasgow Outcome Scores (GOS).
